EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tornado touched down in Walton County just west of Kings Lake Road and traveled east through a neighborhood along and just north of Paradise Island Drive. The tornado then presumably crossed the northern portion of Kings Lake causing more tree damage to the east of the lake. Along most of the path, EF-0 damage was observed. However, near the beginning of the patch two large trees were uprooted and rated EF-1. Near the end of the path, the tornado caused significant removal of the roofing material of a single family home. The porch was also badly damaged. Winds here were estimated at 95 mph, the highest found in this survey. The tornado then lifted quickly as there was no damage east of U.S 331 which is a swampy inaccessible area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy surface and transport winds combined with near critically low humidity values and ongoing severe to extreme drought conditions created elevated fire danger conditions for northeast and north central Florida especially on February 4th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At the beginning of February, Florida Forest Service reported a wildfire of about 318 acres near State Road 20 that then increased to 400 acres and persisted through February 24th. On February 4th and 6th, the Putnam County Sheriffs Office reported that a combination of thick smoke and fog (smog or superfog) resulted in the closure of State Road 20 in the vicinity of Keuka Road. This closure extended to County Road 315 South to Lake Galilee. Schools were also closed on February 4th and 6th due to school bus route cancellations. On February 10th, Putnam County SO advised that CR-20 A, locally Keuka Road, was closed at Strickland Rd due to heavy smoke from the Pace Ct wildfire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: On February 7th, Marion County Fire Rescue reported a 1 acre wildfire near Ocklawaha which then quickly grew to 172 acres before being 100% contained on February 12th. An unknown number of residences were advised to evacuate due to the wildfire.
